topic.name: Applying the Integration By Parts Twice

question.explanation:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define \[ \begin{align*} u=3x^2 \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 6x\\[5pt] \displaystyle\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \cos (2x) \quad & \Longrightarrow \quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\, \textrm{d}x = \int \cos (2x)\, \textrm{d}x =\dfrac{\sin (2x)}{2}. \end{align*} \]

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get \[ \begin{align*} \int 3x^2\cos (2x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= (3x^2)\left(\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{2}\right) - \int\left(\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{2}\right)\left(6x \right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2} - 3\int_0^{\pi/2} x\sin(2x)\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*} \]

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\sin(2x)\,\textrm{d}x.$ We take \[\begin{align*} u=x &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 1\,,\\ \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} =\sin(2x)&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v = \int \sin(2x) \textrm{d}x = -\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{2}. \end{align*}\]

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives \begin{align} \int x\sin (2x)\,\textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= x\left(-\dfrac {\cos(2x)}{2}\right) -\int\left(-\dfrac {\cos(2x)}{2}\right)\cdot 1\,\mathrm dx\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac {x\cos(2x)}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\int \cos(2x)\,\mathrm dx\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac {x\cos(2x)}{2} + \dfrac {\sin(2x)}{4} + D \end{align} where $D$ is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is \begin{align} \int 3x^2\cos (2x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2} - 3\int x\sin (2x)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2} - 3\left( -\dfrac {x\cos(2x)}{2} + \dfrac {\sin(2x)}{4} + D \right)\\ &= \dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2} + \dfrac {3x\cos(2x)}{2} - \dfrac {3\sin(2x)}{4} + C \end{align}

where $C = -3D.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: \begin{align} \int_0^{\pi/2} 3x^2\cos (2x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \left[\dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2} + \dfrac {3x\cos(2x)}{2} - \dfrac {3\sin(2x)}{4} \right]_0^{\pi/2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)^2\sin(\pi)}{2} + \dfrac {3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cos(\pi)}{2} - \dfrac {3\sin(\pi)}{4} - \left(\dfrac{3(0)^2\sin(0)}{2} + \dfrac {3(0)\cos(0)}{2} - \dfrac {3\sin(0)}{4}\right)\\[5pt] &= 0 + \dfrac{3\pi(-1)}{4}- 0 -0 \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3\pi}{4} \end{align}

example.title: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice

question.explanation:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define \[\begin{align*}u=\ln^2 \left(x^3\right)\quad & \Longrightarrow \quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{6\ln (x^3)}{x}\\[5pt] \displaystyle\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = 1 \quad & \Longrightarrow \quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\, \textrm{d}x = \int\,\textrm{d}x = x.\end{align*}\]

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int \ln^2 \left(x^3\right)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \left(\ln^2 \left(x^3\right)\right)(x) - \int (x)\left(\dfrac{6\ln (x^3)}{x} \right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= x\ln^2 \left(x^3\right) - {6}\int {\ln(x^3)} \,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}\]

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int {\ln(x^3)} \textrm{d}x.$ We take

\[\begin{align*}u=\ln(x^3)\quad &\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{3}{x}\\[5pt] \displaystyle\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = 1\quad & \Longrightarrow\quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} \,\textrm{d}x = \int \,\textrm{d}x = {x}. \end{align*}\]

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives \[\begin{align*} \int \ln(x^3)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \left(\ln(x^3) \right)(x) - \int (x)\left(\dfrac{3}{x} \right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= x\ln(x^3) -3\int \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=x\ln(x^3) -3{x} + D, \end{align*}\] where $D$ is a constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is \[\begin{align*} \int \ln^2 \left(x^3\right) \,\textrm{d}x &= x\ln^2 \left(x^3\right) - 6\left (x\ln(x^3) -{3x} + D\right)\\[5pt] &= x\ln^2 \left(x^3\right) - {6x\ln(x^3)}+{18x} + C, \end{align*}\] where $C = -{6D}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: \[\begin{align*} \int_1^{e} \ln^2 \left(x^3\right) \, \textrm{d}x &=\left[ x\ln^2 \left(x^3\right) - {6x\ln(x^3)}+{18x} \right]_1^e\\[5pt] &=\left[ e\ln^2 \left(e^3\right) - {6e\ln(e^3)}+{18e} \right] - \left[ (1)\ln^2 (1^3) - {6(1)\ln(1^3)}+{18(1)} \right]\\[5pt] &= 9e-18e+18e-18\\[5pt] &= 9e-18.\end{align*}\]

example.title: Computing the Integral of a Logarithmic Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define \[\begin{align*} u=(\ln x)^2 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2\ln x}{x}\,,\\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = 18x^2 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\, \textrm{d}x = \int 18x^2\,\textrm{d}x = 6x^3. \end{align*}\]

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int 18x^2(\ln x)^2 \, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \left(\ln x\right)^2\left(6x^3\right) - \int \left(6x^3\right)\left(\dfrac{2\ln x}{x} \right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 6x^3\left(\ln x\right)^2 -12\int {x^2\ln x}\, \textrm{d}x. \end{align*}\]

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int {x^2\ln x} \, \textrm{d}x.$ We take \[\begin{align*} u=\ln x &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{x}\,,\\[5pt] \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} =x^2&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\, \textrm{d}x = \int x^2 \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{x^3}{3}\,. \end{align*}\]

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives \[\begin{align*} \int x^2\ln{x} \, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} \, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \ln{x}\left( \dfrac{x^3}{3}\right) - \int \left(\dfrac{x^3}{3} \right)\left(\dfrac{1}{x} \right) \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x^3\ln x}{3}-\dfrac{1}{3}\int x^2 \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{x^3\ln x}{3} -\dfrac{x^3}{9} + D, \end{align*}\] where $D$ is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is \[\begin{align*} \int 18x^2(\ln{x})^2 \, \textrm{d}x & = 6x^3\left(\ln x\right)^2 -12\int {x^2\ln x} \, \textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 6x^3\left(\ln x\right)^2 -12\left(\dfrac{x^3\ln x}{3} -\dfrac{x^3}{9} + D\right)\\[5pt] &= 6x^3\left(\ln x\right)^2 - 4x^3\ln x+\dfrac{4x^3}{3} - 12D\\[5pt] &= x^3\left(6\left(\ln x\right)^2 - 4\ln x+\dfrac{4}{3} \right) + C, \end{align*}\] where $C = -12D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral: \begin{align*} \int_1^e 18x^2(\ln x)^2 \textrm{d}x &=\left[ x^3\left(6\left(\ln x\right)^2 - 4\ln x+\dfrac{4}{3} \right) \right]_1^e\\[5pt] &=\left[ e^3\left(6\left(\ln e\right)^2 - 4\ln e+\dfrac{4}{3} \right) \right] - \left[1^3\left(6\left(\ln 1\right)^2 - 4\ln 1+\dfrac{4}{3} \right) \right]\\[5pt] &=\left[e^3\left(6 - 4 + \dfrac{4}{3} \right)\right] - \dfrac{4}{3} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{10e^3 - 4}{3}} \end{align*}

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define \begin{align*} u=27x^2 \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 54x\\[5pt] \displaystyle\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \sin (3x) \quad & \Longrightarrow \quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\, \textrm{d}x = \int \sin (3x)\, \textrm{d}x =-\dfrac{\cos (3x)}{3}. \end{align*}

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get \begin{align*} \int 27x^2\sin (3x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= (27x^2)\left(-\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{3}\right) - \int\left(-\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{3}\right)\left(54x \right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -9x^2\cos(3x) + 18\int x\cos(3x)\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\cos(3x)\,\textrm{d}x.$ We take \begin{align*} u=x &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 1\,,\\ \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} =\cos(3x)&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v = \int \cos(3x) \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{\sin(3x)}{3}. \end{align*}

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives \begin{align} \int x\cos (3x)\,\textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= x\left(\dfrac {\sin(3x)}{3}\right) -\int\left(\dfrac {\sin(3x)}{3}\right)\cdot 1\,\mathrm dx\\[5pt] &= \dfrac {x\sin(3x)}{3} + \dfrac {\cos(3x)}{9} + D, \end{align} where $D$ is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is \begin{align} \int 27x^2\sin (3x)\, \textrm{d}x &= -9x^2\cos(3x) + 18\int x\cos (3x)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -9x^2\cos(3x) + 18\left(\dfrac {x\sin(3x)}{3} + \dfrac {\cos(3x)}{9} + D \right)\\[5pt] &= -9x^2\cos(3x) + 6x\sin(3x) + 2\cos(3x) + C, \end{align} where $C = 18D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral: \begin{align} \int_0^{\pi/3} 27x^2\sin (3x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \left[-9x^2\cos(3x) + 6x\sin(3x) + 2\cos(3x) \right]_0^{\pi/3} \\[5pt] &= 9\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)^2 - 2 - 2\\[5pt] &= \pi^2 - 4\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\pi^2 - 4} \end{align}

example.title: Computing the Integral of a Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define \[ \begin{align*} u=3x^2 \quad &\Longrightarrow \quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 6x\\[5pt] \displaystyle\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \cos (x) \quad & \Longrightarrow \quad v = \int \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\, \textrm{d}x = \int \cos (x)\, \textrm{d}x =\sin (x). \end{align*} \]

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get \[ \begin{align*} \int 3x^2\cos (x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= (3x^2)(\sin(x)) - \int(\sin(x))(6x)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 3x^2\sin(x) - 6\int x\sin(x)\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*} \]

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\displaystyle \int x\sin(x)\,\textrm{d}x.$ We take \[ \begin{align*} u=x &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 1\,,\\ \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} =\sin(x)&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v = \int \sin(x) \textrm{d}x = -\cos(x). \end{align*} \]

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives \begin{align} \int x\sin (x)\,\textrm{d}x &= \int u \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= uv - \int v \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= x(-\cos(x)) - \int(-\cos(x))\cdot 1\,\mathrm dx\\[5pt] &= -x\cos(x) + \int \cos(x)\,\mathrm dx\\[5pt] &= -x\cos(x) + \sin(x) + D, \end{align} where $D$ is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is \begin{align} \int 3x^2\cos (x)\, \textrm{d}x &= 3x^2\sin(x) - 6\int x\sin (x)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 3x^2\sin(x) - 6\left( -x\cos(x) + \sin(x) + D \right)\\[5pt] &= 3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x) + C, \end{align} where $C = -6D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral: \begin{align} \int_0^{\pi} 3x^2\cos (x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \left[3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x) \right]_0^{\pi} \\[5pt] &= \left(3(\pi)^2\sin(\pi) + 6(\pi)\cos(\pi) - 6\sin(\pi)\right) - \left(3(0)^2\sin(0) + 6(0)\cos(0) - 6\sin(0)\right)\\[5pt] &= 0 + 6\pi(-1) - 0 - 0 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-6\pi} \end{align}
